# Introduction

The `stratsampling` package includes a data-generating process (DGP) for comparing stratified and simple random sampling designs.
The examples below show how to generate simulated populations, vary the structure of surrogate prediction error, and run Monte Carlo experiments.


# Generating a simulated population

The `generate_population()` function creates a randomized experiment with $N$ units, potential outcomes, treatment assignment, observed outcomes, and surrogate predictions.
The surrogate predictions are constructed by adding stratum-specific bias and noise to the true outcomes.
This mimics the setting where an LLM or other automated system produces an outcome measure that is correlated with, but not identical to, the human-coded outcome.


```{r}
set.seed( 42 )
dat <- generate_population(N = 2000,
                           n_strat = 5,
                           tau = 0.5,
                           bias = "moderate",
                           residual_var = "heterogeneous",
                           R2_target = 0.7,
                           strata_config = "balanced-approx",
                           seed = 42)
head( dat )
```

The returned data frame contains:

- `Z`: Treatment indicator (0/1).
- `strata`: Stratum assignment (integer 1 to `n_strat`).
- `Y0`, `Y1`: Potential outcomes under control and treatment.
- `Yobs`: The realized outcome under the assigned treatment.
- `Yhat`: Surrogate prediction (Yobs + stratum-specific noise).
- `ID`: Unique unit identifier.

A boxplot of the errors by stratum and treatment arm
gives an immediate visual summary of how the surrogate may be systematically off.
particular, you can see how the distribution of `Y - Yhat` varies across
strata for both treatment arms.

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot( dat, aes( x = strata, 
                  y = Yobs - Yhat, color = factor(Z),
                  group = interaction(Z,strata) ) ) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs( x = "Stratum x Treatment arm", y = "Surrogate prediction (Yhat)",
        color = "Treatment (Z)" ) +
  theme( axis.text.x = element_text( angle = 45, hjust = 1 ) ) +
  geom_hline( yintercept = 0 ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

For this particular DGP, we see systematic bias in some of the strata, and  more variation in the size of error across strata.

# Simulation factors

The DGP is controlled by several parameters that govern the structure
of the surrogate predictions.
We walk through some of the core ones in the following.

## Surrogate accuracy (`R2_target`)

The `R2_target` parameter controls the overall predictive accuracy of
the surrogate. Higher values mean the surrogate is a better predictor
of the true outcome. The package calibrates the noise so that the
population R-squared of the surrogate approximately matches the target.

```{r, fig.height=3}
scenarios <- tibble(
  R2 = c(0.3, 0.6, 0.9),
  label = paste0("R2 = ", c(0.3, 0.6, 0.9))
)

dat_r2 <- map_dfr(scenarios$R2, function(r2) {
  d <- generate_population(N = 2000, n_strat = 5, tau = 0,
                           bias = "none",
                           residual_var = "homogeneous",
                           R2_target = r2, seed = 42, no_tx = TRUE)
  d$R2_label <- paste0("R2 = ", r2)
  d
})

ggplot(dat_r2, aes(x = Yhat, y = Yobs)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1, size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~R2_label) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "Surrogate accuracy at different R2 targets",
       x = "Surrogate (Yhat)", y = "True outcome (Yobs)")
```


## Bias pattern (`bias`)

The `bias` parameter controls whether the surrogate over- or
under-predicts the true outcome differently across strata. Available
options are:

- `"none"`: No systematic bias in any stratum.
- `"small"`: Bias up to 25% of the outcome standard deviation.
- `"moderate"`: Bias up to 50% of the outcome SD.
- `"large"`: Bias up to 100% of the outcome SD.
- `"extreme-contrast"`: Bias concentrated in only two strata.

Bias is always mean-centered across strata (weighted by stratum size),
so the overall surrogate mean equals the overall true mean on average.

```{r, fig.height = 3}
bias_scenarios <- c("small", "moderate", "large",
                    "extreme-contrast")
dat_bias <- map_dfr(bias_scenarios, function(b) {
  d <- generate_population(N = 3000, n_strat = 5, tau = 0,
                           bias = b,
                           residual_var = "homogeneous",
                           R2_target = 0.7, seed = 42, no_tx = TRUE)
  d$bias_level <- b
  d
})

dat_bias %>%
  group_by(bias_level, strata) %>%
  summarise(bias = mean(Yhat - Yobs), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(bias_level = factor(bias_level, levels = bias_scenarios)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(strata), y = bias, fill = factor(strata))) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~bias_level) +
  labs(title = "Stratum-level bias under different bias settings",
       x = "Stratum", y = "Mean bias (Yhat - Yobs)",
       caption ="'none' omitted as there is nothing to see") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


## Residual variance heterogeneity (`residual_var`)

The `residual_var` parameter controls whether prediction errors (not including bias) are
equally variable across strata or concentrated in certain strata:

- `"homogeneous"`: Equal residual variance in all strata.
- `"heterogeneous"`: Linearly increasing variance across strata.
- `"extreme-contrast"`: One stratum with very high variance and one with
  very low variance (requires at least 3 strata).

```{r, fig.height = 3}
var_scenarios <- c("homogeneous", "heterogeneous", "extreme-contrast")
dat_var <- map_dfr(var_scenarios, function(v) {
  d <- generate_population(N = 3000, n_strat = 5, tau = 0,
                           bias = "none",
                           residual_var = v,
                           R2_target = 0.7, seed = 42, no_tx = TRUE)
  d$var_pattern <- v
  d
})

dat_var %>%
  group_by(var_pattern, strata) %>%
  summarise(resid_sd = sd(Yhat - Yobs), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(var_pattern = factor(var_pattern, levels = var_scenarios)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(strata), y = resid_sd, fill = factor(strata))) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~var_pattern) +
  labs(title = "Residual SD across strata under different variance patterns",
       x = "Stratum", y = "Residual SD") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


## Strata configuration (`strata_config`)

The `strata_config` parameter controls stratum sizes:

- `"balanced-exact"`: Equal sizes (requires `N` divisible by `n_strat`).
- `"balanced-approx"`: Approximately equal via random assignment.
- `"unbalanced"`: Random proportions drawn from a uniform distribution.


# Inspecting the DGP

The `describe_population()` function summarizes a generated dataset.
It gives two tables, one of strata-level characteristics and one of overall population characteristics.

```{r}
describe_population(n_strat = 5,
                    bias = "moderate",
                    residual_var = "heterogeneous",
                    R2_target = 0.7,
                    verbose = TRUE)
```

This method is useful for verifying that the DGP produces the intended
properties before running a large simulation.


# Running a simulation study

A simulation study draws many populations (or samples from a fixed
population) and compares estimator performance. Here we demonstrate
a simple simulation comparing four estimators:

1. **Subset**: Uses only the coded subsample (ignores the surrogate).
2. **SRS**: Model-assisted estimator under simple random sampling.
3. **Stratified**: Model-assisted estimator under proportional
   stratified sampling.
4. **Stratified-Opt**: Model-assisted estimator under Neyman (optimal)
   allocation.

```{r}
# Generate a single population
pop <- generate_population(N = 2000, n_strat = 5, tau = 0.5,
                           bias = "moderate",
                           residual_var = "heterogeneous",
                           R2_target = 0.7,
                           strata_config = "balanced-approx",
                           seed = 1234)

# One iteration function
one_iter <- function(pop, n_code) {
  N <- nrow(pop)

  # --- Subset estimator (SRS, no surrogate) ---
  samp_srs <- pop %>% group_by(Z) %>% sample_n(n_code / 2)
  pop_sub <- pop %>% mutate(S = ifelse(ID %in% samp_srs$ID, 1, 0))
  out_subset <- est_subset(pop_sub, S = pop_sub$S)

  # --- SRS model-assisted ---
  out_srs <- est_ma_srs(pop_sub, Yhat = pop_sub$Yhat, S = pop_sub$S)

  # --- Proportional stratified ---
  pop$S <- generate_sample_index(pop, n_code, Z = "Z", strata = "strata")
  out_strat <- est_ma_strat(pop, Yhat = "Yhat", S = "S",
                             Z = "Z", strata = "strata")

  # --- Optimal stratified ---
  pop_opt <- calc_optimal_allocation_oracle(pop, n_code,
                                             strata = "strata", Z = "Z")
  out_opt <- est_ma_strat(pop_opt, Yhat = "Yhat", S = "S",
                           Z = "Z", strata = "strata")

  bind_rows( Subset = out_subset, 
             SRS = out_srs, 
             Stratified = out_strat, 
             `Stratified-Opt` = out_opt, .id = "method" )
}
```

Now run 200 iterations and summarize:

```{r, cache = FALSE}
set.seed(999)
n_code <- 200

results <- map_dfr(1:200, function(i) {
  out <- one_iter(pop, n_code)
  out$iter <- i
  out
})
```

Then summarize the results:

```{r}
sim_summary <- results %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_est = mean(est),
    bias = mean(est) - 0.5,
    empirical_SE = sd(est),
    mean_SEhat = mean(SEhat),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((est - 0.5)^2)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

sim_summary
```


## A quick multifactor simulation

To understand how different factors affect estimator performance, loop over a grid of DGP settings.
Here we vary `R2_target` and `bias`:

```{r, cache = FALSE}
grid <- expand_grid(
  R2 = c(0.3, 0.6, 0.9),
  bias = c("none", "moderate", "large")
)

grid_results <- map_dfr(1:nrow(grid), function(g) {
  pop_g <- generate_population(N = 2000, n_strat = 5, tau = 0.5,
                                bias = grid$bias[g],
                                residual_var = "heterogeneous",
                                R2_target = grid$R2[g],
                                strata_config = "balanced-approx",
                                seed = 42)

  map_dfr(1:100, function(i) {
    out <- one_iter(pop_g, n_code = 200)
    out$R2 <- grid$R2[g]
    out$bias_level <- grid$bias[g]
    out$iter <- i
    out
  })
})

```

Results in hand, summarize by factor combination

```{r}
factor_summary <- grid_results %>%
  group_by(R2, bias_level, method) %>%
  summarise(RMSE = sqrt(mean((est - 0.5)^2)),
            .groups = "drop")
```

Then simply plot the results:

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
factor_summary %>%
  mutate(bias_level = factor(bias_level,
                              levels = c("none", "moderate", "large"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = R2, y = RMSE, color = method)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.02, height = 0 ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ bias_level,
             labeller = labeller(R2 = function(x) paste0("R2 = ", x),
                                  bias_level = function(x) paste0("Bias: ", x))) +
  labs(title = "RMSE across simulation factors",
       x = "R2", y = "RMSE") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```
